items.title: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark
items.description: A new beginning for Windows PCs starts tomorrow with the launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark — one PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. items.content: A new beginning for Windows PCs starts tomorrow with the launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark — one PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. All are invited to celebrate with NVIDIA and partners at launch events around the world. Share Your Spark Every PC has a story. What was your first Windows PC, and what did it spark a love for? Join the celebration online by sharing responses with #ShareYourSpark for a chance to win an ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark laptop signed by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. See the campaign and official rules. See What Reviewers Are Saying From local AI workflows to creative apps and gaming, see what reviewers are saying about RTX Spark — then experience it at a launch celebration. “The fact that NVIDIA, Microsoft and their partners have delivered such a capable, compatible and polished platform even in its first at-bat should put the rest of the PC industry on notice.” — Tom’s Hardware “I tested NVIDIA’s RTX Spark for gaming and local AI – the performance absolutely stunned me.” — TrustedReviews, UK “I’m very happy to report that performance is actually looking really good when it comes to AI, gaming and creative workflows.” — Microcenter “[RTX Spark] is a different species of computer that has arrived early. It is a statement of intent from NVIDIA about where computing is going — trading raw benchmarking crowns for the ability to carry a self-rewriting, fully autonomous, CUDA-accelerated digital brain in your backpack.” — Tom’s Guide “One of the most impressive parts of the launch is how many apps NVIDIA has worked with to ensure optimisation with the Spark technology.” — Creative Bloq Independent testing from Artificial Analysis offers an early look at the powerful local AI performance RTX Spark brings to a laptop. Join the Launch Celebrations On Friday, Oct. 16, get hands on with RTX Spark at launch events around the world. Explore demos for creating, developing and gaming, connect with fellow enthusiasts and discover what local AI can do. Times below are local. Follow each event’s entry instructions. Space is limited. San Francisco — Best Buy, 1717 Harrison Street, 10 a.m.-12 p.m. Try hands-on demos, meet iJustine and hear fireside conversations with local tech founders. Free, first-come, first-served entry; no ticket required. Event details. Berlin — Xperion at Saturn, Alexanderplatz 3, 7-10:30 p.m. Explore hands-on demos and stage programming with creators and developers. Registration required. RSVP. Taipei — Muse Garden, No. 88 Yanchang Road. Join an evening of demos, music and AI community discussions, with shopping and networking continuing until 10:15 p.m. Registration required. Beijing — JD MALL Beijing Shuangjing Store, No. 31 Guangqu Road. Check in begins at 7 p.m. Launch celebration starts at 8 p.m., followed by hands-on demos. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. Register through WeChat. Istanbul — Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı, Mevlana Caddesi No. 138. Explore hands-on demos and local creator programming. Walk-in entry; no advance registration required. Seoul — COEX East Lobby, 513 Yeongdong-daero. Hands-on demos begin at 7 p.m., with gaming and AI creator programming from 8 p.m. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. No advance registration required.
items.author: Shreevar Rastogi
items.titleZh: 见证开端：庆祝NVIDIA RTX Spark发布
items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA 宣布，Windows PC 的新开端将于明天随 NVIDIA RTX Spark 的发布而开启。RTX Spark 被定位为一款为创作者、游戏玩家和 AI 代理打造的 PC。NVIDIA 与合作伙伴将在全球举办发布庆祝活动，邀请用户参与。发布前，多家媒体已给出评价。活动还包括 #ShareYourSpark：用户可分享自己的第一台 Windows PC 以及它点燃了何种热爱，并有机会赢取一台由 NVIDIA 创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋签名的 ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark 笔记本。

从技术定位看，RTX Spark 的核心并非单纯追求传统基准测试排名，而是把本地 AI、CUDA 加速和 Windows PC 生态结合，面向本地 AI 工作流、创意应用和游戏。Tom’s Guide 称其为“一种提前到来的不同种类计算机”，是 NVIDIA 对计算发展方向的表态：从追逐跑分转向在背包中携带可自我重写、完全自主、CUDA 加速的“数字大脑”。其创新点还包括 NVIDIA 与 Microsoft 及众多应用合作，确保 Spark 技术优化，使平台在首次登场时就有较强兼容性和完成度。不过，新闻未披露具体芯片架构、CUDA 核心数、显存、功耗等核心技术参数。

性能方面，评测者给予积极定性评价。Tom’s Hardware 认为，NVIDIA、Microsoft 及合作伙伴在“第一棒”就交付了强大、兼容且打磨完善的平台，应让 PC 行业其他厂商警觉。TrustedReviews 称在游戏和本地 AI 测试中性能“绝对令人震惊”。Microcenter 表示 AI、游戏和创意工作流性能看起来很好。Creative Bloq 强调 NVIDIA 与大量应用合作优化。Artificial Analysis 的独立测试则提供了 RTX Spark 笔记本本地 AI 性能的早期观察。不过，新闻中没有给出具体跑分、帧率、TOPS 或与竞品的量化对比数据，因此目前只能确认评测风向积极，尚无法进行参数级对比。

技术影响和应用场景上，RTX Spark 被视为 Windows PC 的新起点，可能推动本地 AI 代理、创意生产和游戏在移动 PC 上更实用。其目标场景包括本地 AI 工作流、创意应用、游戏、开发以及 AI 代理。若其本地 AI 性能如评测所言，将减少对云端算力的依赖，让更自主的 AI 体验在个人设备上运行。

发布庆祝活动于 10 月 16 日（周五）在全球多地举行，均为当地时间。旧金山在 Best Buy（Harrison Street）上午 10 点至中午，有实操演示、iJustine 参与及本地科技创始人炉边对话，免费、先到先得；柏林在 Xperion at Saturn 晚 7 点至 10 点半，需注册；台北在 Muse Garden 举办晚间演示、音乐和 AI 社区讨论，需注册；北京在 JD MALL 双井店晚 7 点签到、8 点开始、9 点半结束，通过微信注册；伊斯坦布尔在 Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı 可直接入场；首尔在 COEX East Lobby 晚 7 点演示、8 点游戏和 AI 创作者节目，9 点半结束，无需提前注册。活动空间有限，部分需按各活动指引入场。

items.title: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops
items.description:

items.content: Microsoft and Nvidia held a launch party for the first wave of RTX Spark laptops last week in San Francisco, where a new wave of AI PCs took center stage amid a packed crowd and a lively hands-on area. A day after the media event, I was invited to a quieter Nvidia event to hear a lot more about the new RTX Spark computing platform. While Nvidia’s new laptops might look like regular Windows machines, the chips inside are Arm-based, instead of the traditional x64 architecture used by AMD and Intel. Combined with a powerful GPU, RTX Spark is designed for the future of AI, and it means a lot of work has gone into getting these laptops ready for launch.One of the biggest challenges was getting Windows ready for AI agents and local AI models. The big selling point of RTX Spark is the combination of Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU, and unified memory to enable powerful AI models to run on a laptop, so the experience of setting up an AI agent needs to be quick and easy.“When users get into Windows for the first time, they’ll see a new Get Started experience that will launch on an RTX Spark laptop that allows them to find the agent they want, get started with that agent, install it, and get to that agent in only two clicks,” says Peter Dawoud, principal program manager at Microsoft.Agents can be installed and updated through the Windows Store, so you don’t have to worry about finding updates or figuring out what dependencies each one needs. “We’ll continue to develop it and add more features so that agents can offer a whole new bunch of experiences coming through Windows,” Dawoud says.Hermes, Perplexity, and OpenClaw are the first three officially supported agents in Windows at the launch of RTX Spark, but Microsoft is working on bringing others on board. That will presumably eventually include Muse, which Meta announced last week is coming to Windows at some point in the future.Getting started with Hermes was mostly a two-click experience in my testing, but I did run into trouble getting OpenClaw set up properly. The app kept complaining that a local gateway hadn’t been installed properly, and it took an uninstall and reinstall to get everything working fully.I’ve been using OpenClaw for a variety of tasks over the past week, but it’s going to take a lot more testing to really understand the value of this local AI support beyond obvious tasks like coding. Powerful as the RTX Spark chip is, large local models are still a lot slower at responding to prompts than cloud models, so I get the feeling that I’ll use this more for tasks I want to run overnight or leave processing in the background.Microsoft has also done a lot of work behind the scenes to optimize Nvidia’s RTX Spark chips for all the things you’d expect to do on a Windows laptop. Unlike an Intel or AMD laptop, RTX Spark laptops make use of Microsoft’s Prism emulator for apps that don’t have a native Arm version.Emulation was a problem on Windows on Arm for more than a decade, but the launch of Qualcomm’s first Snapdragon X series laptops a couple of years ago has helped RTX Spark laptops now benefit from a variety of Arm-native apps and Microsoft’s improved emulator.There’s still a lot of tweaking required for Nvidia’s new chips, though. “Emulation isn’t generic. Each platform needs tuning,” says Dawoud. ”Each core is different. How we translate x64 to that core needs to be highly optimized, and for RTX Spark we’ve done a lot of work to optimize for its microarchitecture.”Some of that optimization has been focused on gaming, particularly because CPUs often dictate frame pacing of games and how smooth they feel, while a GPU does the heavy lifting of rendering the game. Microsoft is quietly shipping Prism updates all the time. “Every month we ship an update to improve compatibility,” says Dawoud. “It’s something we’re constantly working on at the Windows team.”Microsoft has been focused on memory optimization for RTX Spark laptops, too. Microsoft’s own Surface Laptop Ultra can ship with up to 128GB of unified memory, making it possible to load huge models into memory. “We made incredible investments in Unified Memory Architecture to enable you to load as much as possible into the 128GB,” says Dawoud. “But we are also conserving a little bit of space to make sure the system maintains its responsiveness, and the applications running on top of Windows continue to run well and continue to be responsive.”Microsoft has completed optimizations for how memory works on RTX Spark, including tuning for power and performance, maximizing battery life, and ensuring that you can run a game while rendering a video in the background. You can even manually adjust how much of the unified memory is dedicated to the GPU side with a slider in Nvidia’s Windows app.This slider is useful if you have an RTX Spark laptop with 24GB or 32GB of memory, so you can balance more to the GPU for particular apps and games. While Microsoft and Nvidia maintain that RTX Spark laptops shouldn’t be considered gaming machines, they’re more than capable of running the latest AAA titles.“Nvidia and Microsoft have expended a lot of energy over the last many, many, many, many months trying to think deeply about making sure that RTX Spark can deliver a true form of RTX gaming experience,” says Dawoud.One of the first parts of making sure RTX Spark supports gaming was getting anti-cheat vendors on board with Windows on Arm. Some of that work started with Qualcomm, but it has clearly accelerated with Nvidia’s involvement.Fortnite, Marvel Rivals, Arc Raiders, Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, and many other games that have anti-cheat engines will be supported out of the box on RTX Spark laptops. Nvidia and Microsoft are also working with a variety of other anti-cheat providers to make more games available in the future.Activision’s Ricochet anti-cheat engine, used in Call of Duty, will support RTX Spark at some point in 2027, and EA has committed to getting its Javelin anti-cheat working in Battlefield in early 2027. PUBG will start working on RTX Spark laptops in the first half of 2027, and Riot Games has committed to getting League of Legends and Valorant running on RTX Spark laptops at some point in the future.Microsoft is also bringing its advanced shader delivery system to RTX Spark. This allows the Xbox app to preload game shaders during download. It’s the same experience that’s been available on Xbox Ally devices, allowing you to download a game, click launch, and have shaders automatically precompiled so you don’t have to sit there and wait to play.I haven’t run into many game compatibility issues during my testing, even though nearly every game I’ve tested has run emulated. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon chips just weren’t powerful enough on the GPU side to make gaming a reality, but Nvidia has put a much more powerful GPU inside the RTX Spark.Your mileage in gaming is going to vary depending on the title, but for the most part I’ve found that medium settings, running at 1440p and DLSS performance, will get you to a stable 60fps in most games. In some titles you may need to drop the resolution or settings lower, though. This definitely isn’t as good as a dedicated gaming laptop, but for something that’s roughly on the level of a MacBook Pro it’s more than good enough for gaming on the go.The last part of Microsoft’s work on RTX Spark involves Windows features. Surprisingly, Copilot Plus PC features like Recall aren’t available on RTX Spark devices at launch. It’s not clear why they’re delayed, but it sounds like they won’t be available fully until next year. “We are partnering closely with Nvidia to deliver Copilot Plus PC experiences on RTX Spark, expected to first become available to Windows Insiders later this year,” says Adrienne Brewbaker, senior director of Windows marketing.Microsoft is also working on a new Windows Search interface that may work best on devices like the RTX Spark and other Copilot Plus PCs. The interface is being overhauled to focus on speed, and even includes actions that let you do things like turn Bluetooth on or off right from the search bar. It essentially turns Windows Search into a launcher, a much-needed improvement. “We think you’ll love it,” says Dawoud. “We think it’ll change the way people interact with Windows.”The padXbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports. Retro gaming is booming at the moment thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience. Microsoft is leaning into this effort with a new Xbox Labs group that’s a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” according to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.” Part of this also seems to be about using AI inside Xbox, as Sharma notes games share many of the same properties as the workloads AI agents have been tackling on the coding side of things.Microsoft has a new machine learning tool to improve weather forecasts. Microsoft claims to have solved old-school physics-based weather forecasting with machine learning. Researchers at the company say they’ve found a new, cost-effective way to make weather forecasts more accurate two to six weeks in advance. Microsoft has even open-sourced the tool it’s using and published the findings in the journal Nature.Honey, Xbox shrunk its controller. Microsoft surprised everyone this week with some new Xbox hardware. The Xbox Nano controller is the company’s smallest controller yet, designed for younger players, smaller hands, and gaming on the go. At $49.99, it’s also more affordable than the regular Xbox controller. It’s around 5 inches in length and includes Xbox wireless and Bluetooth support for connecting to Xbox consoles and phones, tablets, and PCs. The Xbox Nano controller also includes a rechargeable battery and doesn’t require AA batteries or a separate charging pack like most Xbox controllers. You can preorder the Xbox Nano now, and it will start shipping in November.Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs. Microsoft announced its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip this week, and it’s not all about beating Amazon or Google anymore. This time around the Maia 300 improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, and it’s also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks. These advances will soon make Maia the “primary AI interference system” for Microsoft’s products and services, making the company less reliant on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD.Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are “compromised.” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella published a lengthy post on X over the weekend that laid out his views on the dangers of advanced AI models. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice and actions we simply accept or reject. He calls for building a more transparent system where models can be contained, observed, and leave behind “tamper-proof human readable evidence.” Nadella’s recommendations are thoughtful and well balanced, but unfortunately they were overshadowed by his use of “Super Intelligence” instead of AI. That’s what President Donald Trump wants companies to call AI, and it seems Microsoft is toeing the line.Microsoft launches its new AI model for making decisions quickly. Microsoft has announced its new Microsoft-Decision-1 model just days after OpenAI revealed its new Decisions API. The model is designed to choose the most efficient AI model to complete a task, and Microsoft claims it beats others in tests to determine speed and accuracy.Microsoft 365 Family subscribers will finally be able to share AI benefits. Microsoft is about to let Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers share Copilot and AI usage features, alongside access to Office apps and OneDrive storage, with up to five other people on a plan. The bad part? Instead of getting 1TB of OneDrive storage per account, Microsoft is now limiting this to just 2TB of shared storage across the entire plan. Microsoft argues this makes storage more flexible if one member exceeds 1TB, but it looks like it’s an easy way for the company to upsell more OneDrive storage in reality.Forza Horizon 6 is being delayed on PS5 to January 2027. I reported last month that Forza Horizon 6’s PS5 release would be delayed to early 2027, and now Playground Games has officially confirmed the game will debut on January 26th. The delay means the PS5 version will now coincide with a new expansion for the game. Playground Games will also sell a Premium Edition of Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 that offers up to five days of early access ahead of January 26th.Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages. Hopefully you’ll start seeing fewer scam texts about parking fines or fake deliveries, as Microsoft says it has helped dismantle a marketplace for scammers. Together with Japan’s National Police Agency, Microsoft tracked scam activity back to a marketplace called YAM Store and some phishing kits that helped scammers send messages. Microsoft says it disabled over 20,000 accounts connected to YAM Store and blocked over 100,000 web domains being used for impersonation and fraud.The Link to Windows app for Android might soon let you shut down your PC remotely. You can already lock your Windows PC through the Link to Windows app, but it looks like you’ll soon be able to shut it down remotely, too. An updated beta version has a new power menu with options to lock, sleep, shut down, or restart a PC.How Gears of War: E-Day solves the Xbox Series S memory issue by tapping the SSD. The Coalition has created a solution for working around the 10GB of memory limit on Microsoft’s smaller Xbox Series S console. We’ve heard plenty of stories over the years about how this memory limit has been difficult at times for developers, and now a bespoke system designed in collaboration with the Xbox platform team and Advanced Technology Group has allowed E-Day to use the SSD as a new tier of memory. The technique has allowed The Coalition to keep the game’s density high on the Series S, instead of lowering the quality.Microsoft’s science president is leaving after 16 years. There are few people who have had such an impact inside Microsoft as Peter Lee. The president of Microsoft Science is resigning for a “once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to join an elite team,” in what he says is a “major detour” from the work he has been doing over the past 20 years. Lee has always been the main face of Microsoft Research, and he led the company’s research operations across 14 worldwide laboratories over the past four years. I’m not sure where this leaves Microsoft Research, but it definitely leaves Microsoft without another talented executive.I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. I’m also tomwarren on Telegram, if you’d prefer to chat there.Thanks for subscribing to Notepad.

items.titleZh: Windows 如何为 Nvidia 的 RTX Spark 笔记本电脑进行优化
items.descriptionZh:
微软与英伟达上周在旧金山为首批RTX Spark笔记本电脑举办了发布会，新一代AI PC成为全场焦点。RTX Spark是英伟达全新的计算平台，其笔记本外观与普通Windows设备无异，但内部搭载的是基于Arm架构的芯片，而非AMD和英特尔传统使用的x64架构。结合强大的GPU，RTX Spark专为AI未来而设计，这意味着大量工作投入到了让这些笔记本做好上市准备中。

最大的挑战之一是让Windows为AI智能体和本地AI模型做好准备。RTX Spark的核心卖点是Arm CPU、Blackwell GPU和统一内存的组合，使强大的AI模型能够在笔记本上运行，因此设置AI智能体的体验必须快速简便。微软首席项目经理Peter Dawoud表示，用户首次进入Windows时会看到全新的"Get Started"体验，只需两次点击就能找到想要的智能体、开始使用、安装并进入该智能体。智能体可通过Windows Store安装和更新，用户无需担心查找更新或确定依赖项。Hermes、Perplexity和OpenClaw是RTX Spark上市时Windows首批官方支持的三个智能体，微软正在引入更多智能体，预计最终将包括Meta此前宣布将登陆Windows的Muse。在实际测试中，Hermes的启动基本是两次点击的体验，但OpenClaw的设置遇到了问题，应用反复提示本地网关未正确安装，需要卸载重装才能完全正常工作。虽然RTX Spark芯片性能强大，但大型本地模型响应提示的速度仍远慢于云端模型，因此更适合用于过夜运行或后台处理的任务。

微软还在幕后做了大量工作，针对Windows笔记本上各种预期用途优化英伟达RTX Spark芯片。与英特尔或AMD笔记本不同，RTX Spark笔记本对没有原生Arm版本的应用使用微软的Prism模拟器。模拟问题在Windows on Arm上困扰了十多年，但两年前高通首批Snapdragon X系列笔记本的推出，使RTX Spark笔记本如今受益于丰富的Arm原生应用和微软改进后的模拟器。不过英伟达新芯片仍需大量调优。Dawoud表示，模拟并非通用方案，每个平台都需要调优，每个核心都不同，如何将x64翻译到该核心需要高度优化，微软为RTX Spark的微架构做了大量优化工作。部分优化聚焦于游戏，因为CPU通常决定游戏的帧节奏和平滑度，而GPU负责繁重的渲染工作。微软持续发布Prism更新，每月推出改进兼容性的更新。

微软还专注于RTX Spark笔记本的内存优化。微软自家的Surface Laptop Ultra可配备高达128GB统一内存，能够加载巨大模型。Dawoud表示，微软在统一内存架构上投入巨大，使用户能尽可能多地加载到128GB中，但也保留部分空间以确保系统保持响应性，Windows上运行的应用继续良好运行。微软已完成RTX Spark内存工作方式的优化，包括功耗和性能调优、最大化电池续航，以及确保可以一边运行游戏一边在后台渲染视频。用户甚至可以通过英伟达Windows应用中的滑块手动调整统一内存分配给GPU的比例，这对配备24GB或32GB内存的RTX Spark笔记本尤为有用。

虽然微软和英伟达坚称RTX Spark笔记本不应被视为游戏机，但它们完全有能力运行最新的AAA大作。Dawoud表示，英伟达和微软在过去很多个月里投入了大量精力，深入思考如何确保RTX Spark能提供真正的RTX游戏体验。确保RTX Spark支持游戏的首要工作之一是让反作弊厂商支持Windows on Arm。部分工作始于高通，但随着英伟达的参与明显加速。《堡垒之夜》《漫威争锋》《ARC Raiders》《反恐精英2》《Dota 2》等众多带反作弊引擎的游戏将在RTX Spark笔记本上开箱即用。英伟达和微软还在与多家反作弊提供商合作，未来将支持更多游戏。动视的Ricochet反作弊引擎（用于《使命召唤》）将在2027年某个时候支持RTX Spark，EA承诺在2027年初让Javelin反作弊在《战地》中运行，PUBG将在2027年上半年支持RTX Spark笔记本，Riot Games承诺未来让《英雄联盟》和《无畏契约》在RTX Spark笔记本上运行。微软还将先进着色器交付系统引入RTX Spark，允许Xbox应用在下载期间预加载游戏着色器，与Xbox Ally设备上的体验相同，下载游戏后点击启动即可自动预编译着色器，无需等待。

在实际测试中，尽管几乎所有测试游戏都是模拟运行，但游戏兼容性问题并不多。高通的骁龙芯片在GPU方面不够强大，无法实现真正的游戏体验，但英伟达在RTX Spark中内置了更强大的GPU。游戏体验因游戏而异，但大多数情况下，中等设置、1440p分辨率加DLSS性能模式可在多数游戏中达到稳定60fps，部分游戏可能需要降低分辨率或设置。这虽然不如专用游戏笔记本，但对于大致相当于MacBook Pro水平的设备来说，足以满足移动游戏需求。

微软在RTX Spark上的最后一部分工作涉及Windows功能。令人意外的是，Recall等Copilot Plus PC功能在RTX Spark设备上市时并不可用，延迟原因不明，但似乎要到明年才能完全提供。微软Windows营销高级总监Adrienne Brewbaker表示，微软正与英伟达密切合作，在RTX Spark上提供Copilot Plus PC体验，预计今年晚些时候首先向Windows Insiders开放。微软还在开发新的Windows搜索界面，可能在RTX Spark等Copilot Plus PC上表现最佳。该界面正围绕速度进行 overhaul，甚至包含可直接从搜索栏开启或关闭蓝牙等操作，实质上将Windows搜索变为一个启动器。

新闻后半部分还涵盖了一系列微软相关动态：Xbox正式成立新的Xbox Labs小组，拥抱AI驱动的游戏移植浪潮；微软发布新的机器学习天气预测工具并开源，声称已用机器学习解决传统物理天气预测问题，可提前两到六周提供更准确的预报；Xbox推出最小的Xbox Nano控制器，售价49.99美元，11月开始发货；微软发布第三代自研AI芯片Maia 300，提升云端AI工作负载的成本和效率，将使其减少对英伟达和AMD GPU的依赖；微软CEO纳德拉发帖阐述对先进AI模型危险的看法，呼吁建立更透明的系统，但其使用"超级智能"而非"AI"的措辞引发关注；微软发布新的Microsoft-Decision-1模型，用于快速选择最高效的AI模型完成任务；Microsoft 365 Family订阅者将能共享Copilot和AI使用权益，但OneDrive存储改为全计划共享2TB；《极限竞速：地平线6》PS5版延期至2027年1月26日；微软与日本警方合作捣毁发送超十亿条诈骗信息的网络犯罪市场YAM Store，禁用超2万个账户并屏蔽超10万个用于冒充和欺诈的域名；Android版Link to Windows应用可能很快支持远程关机；《战争机器：E-Day》通过与Xbox平台团队和先进技术组合作，利用SSD作为新一层内存，解决了Xbox Series S的10GB内存限制问题；微软科学总裁Peter Lee在任职16年后离职。

items.title: Sipeed reveals Chinese-made DGX Spark and Ryzen AI Halo rival, expected to cost $3,999
items.description: Sipeed’s MaixStation pairs Axera’s AX8860P with 128GB of LPDDR5X at 273 GB/s to take on Nvidia’s DGX Spark and AMD’s Ryzen AI Halo.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A Chinese rival to the DGX Spark and the Ryzen AI Halo, at least on paper, has emerged with Sipeed’s announcement of the MaixStation. The system, built on Axera’s new AX8860P, is in the same memory class with 128GB of LPDDR5X on a 256-bit bus at 273 GB/s. Sipeed told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects the 128GB model to cost around $3,999, with launch discounts on Kickstarter, putting it level with the 128GB Ryzen AI Halo and well under the DGX Spark’s current MSRP of $6,950. Sign-ups are open now on Sipeed’s MaixStation page ahead of a Kickstarter campaign at the end of the year, with units shipping within three months after it closes. The NPU toolchain is due by the end of this month.Coming today! Beat DGX Spark! MaixStation soon～ https://t.co/e7DvWweVntOctober 13, 2026The AX8860P is a 16-core Arm Cortex-A55 part with an in-house NPU rated at 256 TOPS at native FP4 with no sparsity. The chip is produced in the 6nm process, Axera says. Sipeed claims the system has 25% faster prefill and 30% faster decode than the DGX Spark when running Qwen 27B (the company did not disclose which specific model, but later details that it expects a single MaixStation to run Qwen 3.8-27B) from a single node.In its email, though, the company put its MaixStation about 10% ahead on both prefill and decode when compared to DGX Spark, with FP4 on each machine, with speculative decoding off, and said newer runs with a wider lead aren’t official yet. It teased the new product on its X account, showing a photo from the AX8860P’s announcement at an industrial fair in Shanghai on Tuesday.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Swipe to scroll horizontally Sipeed MaixStation vs Nvidia DGX Spark vs AMD Ryzen AI Halo Header Cell - Column 0 Sipeed MaixStation (Axera AX8860P) Nvidia DGX Spark (GB10) AMD Ryzen AI Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495) AMD Ryzen AI Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) Status Kickstarter at the end of 2026; specs are Sipeed’s claims 128GB on sale; 64GB due Oct. 23 through partners On sale On sale CPU 16 Arm Cortex-A55 cores 20 Arm cores (10 Cortex-X925, 10 Cortex-A725) 16 Zen 5 cores 16 Zen 5 cores Memory 128GB LPDDR5X; 512GB on MaixStation Pro 128GB LPDDR5X; 64GB through partners 192GB LPDDR5X-8533 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 Memory bandwidth 273 GB/s 273 GB/s 273 GB/s 256 GB/s AI compute (rated peak) NPU: 256 TOPS FP4, no sparsity Blackwell GPU: up to 1 PFLOP FP4 with sparsity, about 500 TFLOPS dense Radeon 8065S GPU (40 CUs): up to 61 TFLOPS FP16; NPU: up to 55 TOPS Radeon 8060S GPU (40 CUs); NPU: up to 50 TOPS Software Debian 13; NPU toolchain due at the end of October; Sipeed claims vLLM, SGLang and PyTorch support DGX OS (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) with CUDA and Nvidia’s AI software stack preinstalled ROCm, validated as a “Best-Known Configuration”; Linux now, Windows “coming soon” Linux or Windows 11 Pro Networking 10G SFP+; 256 Gbps C2C link (up to 384 Gbps), up to eight nodes without a switch, per Sipeed 10GbE; ConnectX-7 at 200 Gbps, up to four systems (four need a switch) 10GbE 10GbE Price About $3,999 expected (128GB), per Sipeed $6,950 (128GB); 64GB from $4,999 through partners from Oct. 23 $7,299.99 (Linux) $3,999.99 For comparison, the DGX Spark also comes in 128GB at 273 GB/s with another SKU at 64GB, the two models priced at $6,950 and from $4,999. The former has been on sale since October 2025, at its current price since Oct. 2, and the latter is expected through partners on Oct. 23. For AMD, its Ryzen AI Halo has a 192GB Max+ PRO 495 model at 273 GB/s, released earlier this week at $7,299.99 for the Linux version, and the 128GB Max+ 395 model with 256 GB/s at $3,999.99. In all cases, 256-bit LPDDR5X is used, so the salient differences are memory capacity, compute, and software.Memory is also a big share of what these systems cost: the best U.S. price for a 128GB DDR5 kit was $3,399 in August, and TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise another 10–15% this quarter. As for its unit prices, Sipeed says it used current DRAM prices rather than stock bought last year. It also suggested buyers could supply their own SSD, which could cut the price further, clarifying that the MaixStation takes a standard M.2 2280 drive rather than the Spark’s less common 2242. You may like AMD attempts to get ahead of expected RTX Spark launch with Gorgon Halo benchmarks Nvidia introduces 64GB DGX Spark to throw local AI fans a lifeline amid the RAMpocalypse Early AMD 'Gorgon Halo' AI mini-PC packs 192GB RAM for an eye-watering $7,099 Software-wise, the Spark ships with DGX OS, which is Nvidia’s build of Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, with CUDA and Nvidia’s AI software stack preinstalled. AMD validates ROCm, drivers, models, and frameworks together as a “Best-Known Configuration.” Neither the Spark nor the PRO 495 ships with Windows yet, though AMD says Windows versions are “coming soon,” and the Max+ 395 model already offers Windows 11 Pro. Sipeed, aside from its upcoming NPU toolchain, claims support for vLLM, SGLang, and PyTorch, with Axera adding ONNX, Hugging Face (HF) model formats, and an OpenAI-compatible API. MaixStation itself ships with Debian 13 and Linux 6.18, and Windows support for the PCIe card will depend on demand, Sipeed says.Chinese solutions already exist on AMD silicon, such as GMKtec’s 192GB Evo-X5 Pro at $6,799 to $7,099. There’s also Minisforum’s MS-S1 Max-P495. What’s new with the MaixStation is the Chinese silicon underneath.The Axera AX8860P, as recently launched, has, in addition to the above specs, PCIe 5.0 support, 64-channel video decode with 16-channel encode, and support for multiple form factors, including a single-slot, four-chip PCIe card capable of running up to 512GB of memory, with mini and pocket PC products planned. Like the eight-core AX8850 in Radxa’s and M5Stack’s M.2 accelerator cards, it pairs Arm Cortex-A55 cores with Axera’s NPU, now with twice the cores and up to 128GB of memory instead of 8GB. Two- and four-chip cascades reach a theoretical 512 and 1,024 TOPS, respectively, at a claimed scaling efficiency of about 80%. The CPU, against the Spark’s Cortex-X925 and Halo’s Zen 5, is small and in-order. It’s sufficient for the NPU but potentially more limited for other tasks.The box itself measures about 11 × 11 × 3 cm and draws about 40W in typical use, powered over USB-C, according to Sipeed. Its ports include 10G SFP+, USB-C, an M.2 2280 slot for a PCIe 5.0 SSD, and an MCIO 8i connector for linking a second unit.Sipeed says the MaixStation supports all configurations, that’s single, dual, and quad node, plus any “PCIe card mode for any card count you want.” The interconnect in use is a 256 Gbps C2C connection (up to 384 Gbps) “without [an] extra switch needed, and [up to] 8-node.” What to read next Lenovo ThinkCentre X Ultra packs Gorgon Halo Exploring Apple Silicon’s local AI performance with the Mac Studio and M4 Max Minisforum launches local AI solutions at IFA 2026 The contrast is with the Spark’s QSFP ports, and Nvidia’s datasheet says linking four Sparks “requires [an] external switch.” The math, at 32 Gbps per lane, works out to 256 Gbps with the default eight lanes and 384 Gbps with the maximum of twelve. Remote-access test units and a few review units will follow during the Kickstarter campaign, the company told us.Sipeed also commented on the openness of the platform, saying, “Yes, bsp sdk is open, you can use AI to port any distribution on it!” Sipeed has previously sold Axera boards, with products dating back to 2022 using the AX620A, AX650N, and AX630C.The claims of the MaixStation being faster in some workloads are coupled with Sipeed saying “In fact you need [to] ask why DGX is so slow…” with potential financial implications, as Nvidia “just [wants to make] more money from users.” When an X user argued that Sipeed must be using extreme quantization at that bandwidth, the company suggested that the Spark’s specs may be overstated.By our math, the decode claim is plausible with a 4-bit 27B model, which sits at about 13.5GB. Performance on comparable machines tops out near 20 tokens per second, which means around 270 GB/s. Prefill, which is compute-bound, is a harder sell, but Sipeed stated that “DGX Spark 1000TOPS is fake ‘sparse.’” That 1 PFLOP figure does rely on sparsity, but the DGX Spark’s dense rate of about 500 TFLOPS is still around double the AX8860P’s 256 TOPS.Axera’s current stack has Pulsar2 as the NPU compiler and toolchain, with version 8.0 on HuggingFace last week, and the V7.0 docs already list the chip as the AX8860. There’s no operator support list for the chip yet, and the docs’ LLM chapter for older chips lists weights down to 4-bit integers but no FP4. Neither the ax-llm runtime nor AXCL, the host-side PCIe driver and runtime for Axera’s cards, lists the chip yet. Sipeed says the end-of-month release is AXDSL, a kernel-programming language, plus the Pulsar2 source code, and that SGLang and vLLM run on a custom backend built on it, so Hugging Face models run without a conversion step.Enthusiasts are already eager to know the final specifications and pricing for the different models. On paper, as far as local LLM machines go, the MaixStation matches the Spark on memory size and claimed bandwidth, and the Max+ PRO 495 Halo on bandwidth alone. Testing performance claims will also have to wait for the toolchain and sample machines land, hopefully before the end of the year.
items.author: Shane Downing
items.titleZh: Sipeed发布中国制造DGX Spark与Ryzen AI Halo竞品，预计售价3999美元
items.descriptionZh:
Sipeed 近日发布 MaixStation，定位为 Nvidia DGX Spark 与 AMD Ryzen AI Halo 的中国竞争方案。该系统基于爱芯元智（Axera）新款 AX8860P，配备 128GB LPDDR5X，采用 256-bit 总线，带宽 273 GB/s，并计划提供 MaixStation Pro 的 512GB 版本。Sipeed 向 Tom’s Hardware 表示，128GB 型号预计售价约 3,999 美元，Kickstarter 众筹期间还会有首发折扣；这一价格与 128GB 版 Ryzen AI Halo 相当，但明显低于 DGX Spark 目前 6,950 美元的官方定价。产品预计年底登陆 Kickstarter，众筹结束后三个月内发货，NPU 工具链则计划本月底发布。

核心芯片 AX8860P 采用 6nm 工艺，CPU 为 16 核 Arm Cortex-A55，集成爱芯元智自研 NPU，标称算力 256 TOPS，原生支持 FP4 且不依赖稀疏化。Sipeed 宣称，单节点运行 Qwen 27B 时，MaixStation 的预填充（prefill）比 DGX Spark 快 25%，解码（decode）快 30%；但在后续邮件中，公司把对比收窄为两项均领先约 10%，条件是双方都使用 FP4、关闭投机解码，并表示更大幅领先的新测试“尚非官方数据”。按 Tom’s Hardware 的估算，解码端的说法在 4-bit 27B 模型上具有一定合理性：该模型约占 13.5GB 内存，同类机器性能上限约 20 tokens/s，对应带宽接近 270 GB/s。预填充属于计算密集型任务，挑战更大；Sipeed 还称“DGX Spark 的 1000 TOPS 是虚假的‘稀疏’指标”，但即便按约 500 TFLOPS 的密集算力计算，Spark 仍约为 AX8860P 256 TOPS 的两倍。

横向对比方面，DGX Spark 有 128GB 和 64GB 两个版本，带宽 273 GB/s，128GB 售价 6,950 美元，64GB 版本通过合作伙伴从 10 月 23 日起以 4,999 美元起售。AMD Ryzen AI Halo 中，Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 配备 192GB LPDDR5X-8533，带宽 273 GB/s，Linux 版售价 7,299.99 美元；Ryzen AI Max+ 395 配备 128GB LPDDR5X-8000，带宽 256 GB/s，售价 3,999.99 美元。三者均使用 256-bit LPDDR5X，因此主要差异集中在内存容量、计算能力和软件生态。内存成本也是整机价格的重要部分：美国 128GB DDR5 套件在 8 月的最佳价格曾达 3,399 美元，TrendForce 预计本季度传统 DRAM 合约价还将上涨 10%–15%。Sipeed 称其定价基于当前 DRAM 价格而非去年的库存，并指出用户可以自备 SSD，因为 MaixStation 使用更常见的 M.2 2280 规格，而非 DGX Spark 的 2242。

软件方面，MaixStation 预装 Debian 13 和 Linux 6.18，NPU 工具链本月底推出。Sipeed 宣称支持 vLLM、SGLang 和 PyTorch，爱芯元智则补充支持 ONNX、Hugging Face 模型格式和 OpenAI 兼容 API。DGX Spark 预装 DGX OS（基于 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS），集成 CUDA 和 Nvidia AI 软件栈；AMD 将 ROCm、驱动、模型和框架一起验证为“Best-Known Configuration”。Spark 和 PRO 495 目前都尚未预装 Windows，AMD 称 Windows 版本“即将推出”，而 Max+ 395 型号已提供 Windows 11 Pro。Sipeed 表示，PCIe 卡形态的 Windows 支持将取决于需求。爱芯元智现有工具链以 Pulsar2 作为 NPU 编译器和工具链，上周在 Hugging Face 上发布了 8.0 版本，V7.0 文档已把该芯片列为 AX8860；但该芯片尚无算子支持列表，旧芯片的 LLM 文档只列出低至 4-bit 整数的权重，没有 FP4。ax-llm 运行时和面向爱芯元智板卡的主机侧 PCIe 驱动/运行时 AXCL 也尚未列出该芯片。Sipeed 称月底将发布 AXDSL 内核编程语言及 Pulsar2 源代码，SGLang 和 vLLM 将运行在基于它的自定义后端上，从而无需转换步骤即可运行 Hugging Face 模型。

扩展性和形态方面，AX8860P 还支持 PCIe 5.0、64 路视频解码和 16 路编码，并可做成单槽四芯片 PCIe 卡，最高支持 512GB 内存，未来还计划推出迷你和小型 PC 产品。它与 Radxa、M5Stack 的 M.2 加速卡所用八核 AX8850 类似，都是 Cortex-A55 加爱芯元智 NPU，但 AX8860P 核心数翻倍，内存从 8GB 提升到最高 128GB。双芯片和四芯片级联理论算力分别可达 512 TOPS 和 1,024 TOPS，官方称扩展效率约 80%。不过，与 Spark 的 Cortex-X925 和 Halo 的 Zen 5 相比，AX8860P 的 CPU 核心较小且为顺序执行，足以服务 NPU，但在其他通用任务上可能更受限。整机尺寸约 11×11×3 cm，典型功耗约 40W，通过 USB-C 供电，接口包括 10G SFP+、USB-C、用于 PCIe 5.0 SSD 的 M.2 2280 插槽，以及用于连接第二台设备的 MCIO 8i。Sipeed 称 MaixStation 支持单节点、双节点、四节点以及任意数量的 PCIe 卡模式；互连采用 256 Gbps C2C 连接，最高可达 384 Gbps，最多 8 节点无需额外交换机。相比之下，DGX Spark 使用 QSFP 端口，Nvidia 数据表称连接四台 Spark“需要外部交换机”。按每通道 32 Gbps 计算，默认 8 通道为 256 Gbps，最多 12 通道为 384 Gbps。

市场上已有基于 AMD 芯片的中国方案，例如 GMKtec 的 192GB Evo-X5 Pro，售价 6,799 至 7,099 美元，以及 Minisforum 的 MS-S1 Max-P495；MaixStation 的新意在于底层采用中国芯片。Sipeed 还强调平台开放性，称 BSP SDK 开放，用户甚至可以用 AI 将任何发行版移植上去。该公司此前已销售多款爱芯元智板卡，最早可追溯到 2022 年的 AX620A、AX650N 和 AX630C。围绕性能宣称也存在争议：Sipeed 一边声称 MaixStation 在某些工作负载上更快，一边说“事实上你该问为什么 DGX 这么慢”，并暗示 Nvidia“只是想从用户身上赚更多钱”。当有 X 用户质疑其在有限带宽下必须使用极端量化时，Sipeed 又暗示 Spark 的规格可能被夸大。总体而言，纸面上 MaixStation 在内存容量和标称带宽上追平 DGX Spark，在带宽上追平 Max+ PRO 495；但其真实性能、最终规格和价格，仍需等待工具链和样机落地后才能验证，Sipeed 希望在年底前实现这一目标。

items.title: Benn Jordan on Flock, privacy, and the new surveillance backlash
items.description:
Today, I’m talking with Benn Jordan, musician, YouTuber, researcher, and investigative journalist. You might know Benn from those first two titles — he’s got a prolific discography of experimental music dating back decades.
But in the last couple of years, he’s become a high-profile face in the creator and media spaces for his work investigating Flock Safety, the maker of automatic license plate readers and the software that powers them.
Benn recently testified in front of Congress, at a hearing the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held, dedicated to Flock and other ALPR systems. This hearing felt like the culmination of months and months of growing criticism and bipartisan backlash against Flock — all of which is taking a shape similar to the pushback against AI data centers.



Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here. Not a subscriber? You can sign up here. 
This has led to major fallout for Flock. Hundreds of cities, counties, and other local governments have begun canceling contracts, and Flock is now under investigation by Republican Sen. Josh Hawley. Last week, Reuters reported that Flock plans to cut about 18 percent of its workforce.
So of course I wanted to dig into all of that with Benn, not just because he played a role in that, but because he’s also become in some ways the face of a new front in the broader debate about surveillance and privacy.
A point you’ll hear Benn make is that he doesn’t actually hate Flock as a company — he thinks its posture toward critics has been a colossal PR failure that made it low-hanging fruit, while competitors like Axon and Motorola quietly build the same kind of networks. Instead, Benn now talks to Flock directly, including to its CEO Garrett Langley, and reports security vulnerabilities to the company when he finds them. (As a side note: we have also invited Flock’s CEO on the show; Garrett if you’re listening, we would love to have you.)
Benn says his outreach to the company is an olive branch he’s extended to Flock as part of his goal of working toward real, tangible solutions to surveillance overreach, rather than part of a crusade to tear one single company down.
That’s a real theme throughout our conversation: that Flock and other high profile names in surveillance are just part of the problem — our real focus should be on the interlocking relationship between private industry, government, and law enforcement that prioritizes secrecy over transparency.
We never voted for an insecure network of cameras on every street corner, and we’re certainly not being asked if we’re comfortable with access to this network being given to police officers with a penchant for abusing it. So Benn sees his work on YouTube and with other researchers, civil rights groups, and journalists as an accountability function that forces this conversation to the forefront. And so far, it’s working.

One of the things that I want to see with you on the show, most importantly of all, is to describe what a Flock camera is and what the technology behind the hardware does that makes it new.
Because from watching all the videos that you make, I think, “It’s just an Android phone. They’re just putting a bunch of Android phones around town,” but it’s actually the database and the AI that makes it more dangerous than usual. Describe what the actual Flock hardware is and then how that connects to the system that makes it as controversial as it is.
So ALPRs have existed, I believe, since the 1970s. They started getting used in the United States in the late 80s and 90s. One of the classic ways that they would be used in the 2000s is they would be mounted on a police car. If a police car wanted to run someone’s plate, that way they didn’t have to type it in while they’re driving, and they could run a plate over to dispatch. I personally don’t have any problem with that. I think that makes sense. That’s a decent use. However, you would have issues where you would get plate misreads and then people would get taken out of their car at gunpoint as a result.
Flock is a lot different. Flock basically started a private nationwide network where any police department or city that’s using Flock’s network can opt into it and share their data with it. Police departments across the country can then run a license plate with 30 days of retention on everywhere someone’s been, anywhere in the country, as long as they’re sharing the data. So you would have someone in Texas being able to search somebody’s movement through New York or Atlanta or something like that.
They were doing this — they are doing this — without a warrant. Whereas any type of ALPR data sharing previous to Flock had to go through the National Crime Information Center, which does require a magistrate judge to look at the overall context of a situation and then issue a warrant to allow tracking.
That’s the innovation here. They built the private network, the private database, and convinced a bunch of law enforcement agencies to buy their system and they could opt in. There’s some kind of legal innovation here where by making it a private database, they could just excuse themselves from the warrant process.
But the actual hardware of the cameras is not all that impressive. There’s something about that that I really just want to hone in on. The idea of the Flock camera being the problem is secondary to the Flock network being the problem.
One way that I think about it, in the defense of Flock cameras and even outside of Flock itself, is that it’s all happening in public. This is all in public view. It’s generally the same as arguing that you’re allowed to take a picture anywhere in public. So why can’t they do this?
My argument against that would be if you have a police officer follow someone or go through public traffic cams, which are all over the country, and go through every single public traffic cam and wait for your car to come and then write down when that was there and do that for 30 days, that’s generally a serial killer situation.
The amount of resources that you have to dump into that would have to justify that expense with a very serious crime. But doing that for somebody who stole steaks from a Kroger is very different. What worries me about it is that you might end up with police officers being able to get a lead on a case much easier that doesn’t necessarily need police for society to become safer in a better place, like a nonviolent crime or something that’s not a huge deal, rather than investigating more serious crimes.
That’s the argument that Flock makes, and that proponents of this technology make. We had Jamie Siminoff from Ring on the show, and the argument he would make is if you put enough cameras into certain neighborhoods, you will “zero out crime.” That is a thing that he has said to me in the context of Ring doorbells and floodlight cams.

One of the metaphors I like to use is if you have a supermarket and you put one camera in one aisle where you think that things are going to get stolen, that will probably increase theft in other aisles rather than just assuming that every shoplifter is just going to become a plumber instead, like I’ll be a doctor instead of a shoplifter.
That doesn’t actually deal with the overall problem. If you have a Walmart that has cameras all over it, and then you have a neighborhood store that can’t afford all of those fancy cameras, then maybe the shoplifters and people who would hold up a store will go to that place instead and you have the same thing with cities. You have crime relocation happening.
So, yes, of course, if you put a camera above a street, it’s less likely that a car on that street within the view of the camera will get broken into. But does that make it more likely that a car a block over where there is no camera will get broken into? This is something that has been observable by criminologists, like crime relocation is a real thing. A lot of times effective policing just moves criminals elsewhere.
Selfishly, you could say, “In my subdivision, we have less crime, and I don’t care about anything other than that.” But over time, over the next decade, it doesn’t really work out that way. You end up with more crime overall, or you end up with bigger problems in society. So I would argue with that.
Also, we’ve seen that Ring cameras don’t really reduce crime all that much. You end up being able to see somebody stealing a package off your porch or you end up being able to see somebody breaking into your house. But do they actually increase clearance rates? I would argue I’ve not seen any evidence that they do.
You have to connect them to the nationwide database of license plate readers.
[Laughs] Right, yeah.
If you put a camera everywhere, you can’t relocate anywhere. That’s the argument. It’s the end point of the argument that they are making: “If putting up some cameras would move the crime, putting cameras everywhere would make that impossible and there will be no crime.”
With a lot of that stuff, it’s just like, “If you have a problem, if you’re worried that you’re going to have a porch pirate, if you’re worried that your house is going to be broken into, I’m not sure why you would jump to put cameras all over your house?”
It’s the same thing with cities, like why wouldn’t you just increase your insurance? I would say that like along the lines, like even if the clearance rates were improving, which I’ve not seen evidence of, what does that mean? Does that just mean that we’re putting more nonviolent offenders in prison or through the justice system? Does that actually make society safer?
We’re getting into the trade-offs of using technology to solve social problems. One of the most important trade-offs that you have brought to light repeatedly is that these devices are not secure.
So even if you solve the problem of “you should get a warrant” — or even if Flock responds to the public pressure and says, “We ought to make people type case numbers into the system before they start searching,” which was their big concession recently — even if you get to, “We’re going to control the system a little bit better,” the devices themselves are insecure. The network is insecure.
That means anybody can do almost anything they want with it. You’re a security researcher. Describe how you began digging into the security problems here and what the response has been.
Starting out, I found out that they didn’t, in early 2025, require multi-factor authentication. I also witnessed a police officer logging into Flock from a Wi-Fi network that wasn’t at a police station. Had you told me those things, I wouldn’t believe them. But witnessing it happening made me say, “This is something that needs more looking into.” I started thinking, “It’s probable at that point, because now you have human error.”
If all of these police departments are sharing data with one another, then it could just be the dispatcher, somebody who’s not even deputized, who has a Flock account at a rural Louisiana police department. That person could sell their account or that person could click the wrong link in an email and whatever. I started looking for Flock credentials on the dark web and I found some and they were coming from a Russian vendor.
I started thinking, “How exactly did that happen?” That’s how I met [cybersecurity researcher] Jon Gaines, and we found that a lot of the time there were hardware vulnerabilities in the camera where you could get them to open up a Wi-Fi access point, and then you could get complete control over the Android device and you could root it and have it do whatever you wanted in a way that would be undetectable because it’s happening outside of the Flock ecosystem on the device.
I had found a bunch of Flock cameras with administrative interfaces that were open on the internet. So you could just type in the IP address and then delete footage, or watch footage from 30 days ago. You could even put files on the device and look at all the logs. In all these situations, we found a lot of plain text credentials, things that shouldn’t have been there.
At first the pushback from the company was that I’m a YouTuber and I was doing magic tricks and I’m not a serious security researcher. Reading their own statement about having never been hacked through a Flock camera and then downloading it on my own machine made that indisputable.
